correctness.rationale: Uses a precisely stated published congruence-support theorem for odd n. Unique disjoint parametrizations follow from 2-adic parity and uniqueness of a prime with exponent \(1\pmod4\); congruence restrictions are checked modulo \(24\) and modulo \(8\). Removing higher powers and gcd conditions incurs \(O(\sqrt X)\). Uniform fixed-modulus PNT expansions apply for square factors up to \(Y^{1/8}\), with summable tails \(O(Y^{7/8})\) and logarithmic-moment error \(O(Y/(\log Y)^3)\). Euler products verify the constants. Exact generating-function and factorization checks independently agree, but they do not replace the infinite argument.

value.rationale: Given the motivating recent classification of when odd strongly unimodal counts are 2 mod 4, the frequency and residue dependence of these rare exceptional indices are natural unanswered arithmetic invariants. All four residue classes share the same first-order coefficient yet have different explicit secondary constants with a strict \(3:1:0:0\) bias, and two remain equal to all logarithmic orders. This extra 2-adic structure is not a textbook substitution, arbitrary slice, or restatement of the original support criterion; it is an analytic distribution result with future use in finer congruence-frequency questions.
